info.name: 1KOMMA5° Heartbeat API
info.description:
Reverse-engineered endpoints used by the `onekommafive` Python client.

**Hosts**
- `heartbeat.1komma5grad.com` — main API (systems, energy, EMS, EV, weather, AI optimisations)
- `customer-identity.1komma5grad.com` — user profile and active feature flags
- `auth.1komma5grad.com` — Auth0 OAuth2 (PKCE) token endpoint

**Auth**
All requests except those under `Auth` send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` automatically. Obtain the token interactively via the iOS/Android app or via the `1k5` CLI, then paste it into the `accessToken` collection variable.

The `Auth → Refresh token` request expects a valid `refreshToken` collection variable. The Auth0 Authorization-Code-with-PKCE flow used by the mobile app is not modelled here because it requires an interactive browser step.

**Path variables**
Populate the collection variables `systemId`, `siteId` (usually equal to `systemId`), `customerId`, and `evId` once — every request reuses them via `{{...}}`.

variable.description: Auth0 client_id of the 1KOMMA5° mobile app (public).
Bearer JWT for the Heartbeat / Identity APIs. Paste a fresh one here.
Site UUID. Usually identical to systemId.
User UUID (from GET /api/v1/users/me — used by notification endpoints).

item.name: Auth
item.description: Auth0 OAuth2 endpoints. These do NOT use the collection Bearer auth.

exec: // Auto-store fresh tokens into collection variables.
// so a plain 'Export → Only original data' will not leak them.

request.description: Exchange a stored refresh token for a fresh access token. The attached post-response script writes the new `access_token` (and, if rotated, the `refresh_token`) back into the collection variables automatically. Values are stored in `currentValue` only, never in `initialValue`.

Final step of the Authorization-Code + PKCE flow. The preceding interactive steps (authorize, login, resume) cannot be reproduced in Postman because they involve browser redirects under the mobile-app URL scheme. Use the `onekommafive` Python client to perform a full login, then paste the resulting `access_token` / `refresh_token` into the collection variables.

Returns the authenticated user's profile: id, email, first/last name, phone, status, external_id, and the `connectedSystems` list (all sites the user has access to, with per-site name and address). Use `connectedSystems[i].systemId` to switch between multi-site accounts.
List all systems (sites) the authenticated user has access to.
Single system metadata (v4). Does NOT include `energyTraderActive` / `electricityContractActive` — use the `/details` endpoint for those.

Extended metadata: `empType`, technical contact, embedded customer, smart-meter flags, `earliestMeasurement`, `deviceGateways[]`. Also brings back v2-only `energyTraderActive` / `electricityContractActive`.

Site connection status plus hardware asset inventory: HYBRID inverter, HEAT_PUMP, METER, EV_CHARGER (manufacturer, model, serial, firmware, network). Note: serial field is `serialnumber` (lowercase n).
List of active feature flags (e.g. DYNAMIC_TARIFF, TIME_OF_USE_OPTIMIZATION, SMART_CHARGING). `customerId` comes from `/systems/{id}/details`.

Smart-meter registration details: ENTSO-E control-area EIC, DSO BDEW code, municipality concession fee in EUR/kWh. The DSO code and concession fee come as arrays of historic entries with `validFromDate`/`validUntilDate` — the current entry is typically the first element.

Superset of `Get system` (v4) and `Get system details` (v1). Adds `biddingZone`, `biddingZoneEic`, `empDetails` (gateway pairing info — sensitive), `empReferenceId`, `impactedByEnwg` (EnWG regulatory flag — likely §14a controllable-consumption, but not documented by the API), `gridConnectionPointPhases`, `maxCurrentPerPhaseAmpere`, embedded `customer` block, and — most useful — `emsMode`/`emsState`/`emsStateReasons` (EMS runtime state, not exposed by the other system endpoints). Does NOT include `deviceGateways` — use `/systems/{id}/details` for those. Note: v2 and v3 return byte-identical payloads (verified live) — no reason to switch.

Real-time energy overview. Response nests `liveHeroView` and `summaryCards`. For battery_power prefer `summaryCards.battery.power` (negated; API: negative=charging). For grid_power prefer `summaryCards.grid.power`.

query.description: YYYY-MM-DD (≤ 1 day after `from` for 1h; same day for 15m)

request.description: Timeseries are nested under `timestampedProductionAndConsumption.data`.
Response uses `timeseries[ts].marketPrice` (EUR/kWh) and nested `energyMarket.averagePrice.price.amount` (string).

query.description: OPTIONAL — YYYY-MM-DD only (datetimes with a time component return HTTP 400)

request.description: Aggregated Heartbeat savings (EUR) for a date range. Without params: server-side rolling window (undocumented — neither today nor the current month).

item.name: Prices
item.description: User-configured prices and contractual guarantees. Basis for savings-vs-grid-supplier calculations.

request.description: User-configured prices: `gridEnergyPrice`, `comparisonEnergyPrice` (both EUR/kWh as string), `monthlyBasePrice` (EUR/month).

query.description: REQUIRED — site UUID as a query param (not a path segment)

request.description: Single-value grid-supplier reference price in EUR/kWh. Equivalent to `comparisonEnergyPrice` from `/price-customizations` but without the surrounding envelope.

query.description: REQUIRED. Naming quirk: path takes customerId but the query param is 'systemId' (not customerId, not siteId). Without it → HTTP 400.

request.description: Contractual electricity-price guarantee (`priceGuaranteeValue`, `priceGuaranteeUnit` e.g. 'ct/kWh', `priceGuaranteeVersion` e.g. 'DE_PRICE_GUARANTEE_V2'). Sits on the `customer-identity` host.

item.name: Customer
item.description: Full customer record (v3) — superset of the embedded customer block in `/systems/{id}/details`.

request.description: Full customer profile — adds phone, address, `customerType`, `crmContactId`, `crmBranchLocation` on top of the embedded `SystemCustomer` (which only has id/name/email). Field naming quirks: `contactEmail` (not `email`), `addressCountry` as plain-name string (`"Deutschland"`) not ISO code.

All customer contracts. Typical composition: DYNAMIC_PULSE (electricity), SMART_METER (24-mo notice), HEARTBEAT (0 EUR), ENERGY_TRADER (14.99 EUR/mo). Response is PII-heavy — includes `paymentIban`, delivery/billing addresses, CRM identifiers (Zoho/Lumenaza), a `statusHistory` block, and an embedded `metadata.payload` with the full Zoho booking record. The Python client (`System.get_subscriptions`) maps only the universal contract metadata (type/status/price/dates/notice/renewal/paymentMethod-enum/terms + DYNAMIC_PULSE contract-identity fields) and keeps all PII in `.raw`.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: Recent push/in-app notifications and per-category channel preferences. Both endpoints require the user ID from `User → Get current user` (set the `userId` collection variable).

request.description: Recent push/in-app notifications with `title`, `body`, `type`, `read`, `dismissed`, plus `notificationDetails.meta` (e.g. `{price, dateTime_utc}` for price alerts).

User's notification preferences per category (`CO2_IMPACT`, `BATTERY_SOC`, `BROADCAST_NEW_ELECTRICITY_PRICES`, `SYSTEM_HEALTH`, `ENERGY_MARKET_UPPER_TARGET_REACHED`, `ENERGY_MARKET_LOWER_TARGET_REACHED`, `EV_DYNAMIC_PULSE`, `SYSTEM_DATA_COLLECTION_ENDED`). Empty array per category = not subscribed.
API compatibility matrix: `b2b` (installer/partner) and `b2c` (end-user) `targetVersion` and `minimumSupportedVersion`. Not system-scoped.
Returns `today`, `tomorrow` (temp, precipitation, sunshineMinutes, sunrise/sunset, weatherSymbolId) and `fineGrainedForecasts` (3h slots for 48h). Night symbol IDs = day ID + 100.
`overrideAutoSettings: false` → auto mode. `true` → manual override. Returns 201 on success.
Vehicle-side profiles (chargingMode, targetSoc, schedules). For the physical wallbox hardware use `List wallboxes` below.
Physical wallbox hardware (`gridxHardwareId`, `name`, `assignedEvId`). Distinct from `/devices/evs` which returns the vehicle-side profiles. `assignedEvId` links to an entry in `/devices/evs`.
Lists available `ChargingMode` values for this site. Entries with `disabled: true` are excluded by the client.
Allowed values include `SMART_CHARGE`, `FAST_CHARGE`, `SOLAR_OPTIMIZED`, `MANUAL_CHARGE`, etc. — call `Get displayed charging modes` for the active list.
Target state-of-charge as a decimal in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.8 = 80%).
Decimal in [0, 1]. Only meaningful in `SMART_CHARGE` mode.
Format `HH:MM` (24h).

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Aggregated business metrics — CO2 savings, energy-trader statistics, monthly trading average.

request.description: Lifetime CO2 figures: `co2Savings` (site, kg), `co2CollectiveSavings` (entire 1KOMMA5° customer base, kg), `co2GlobalSavingsEstimate` (marketing figure, tons). Ignores any query parameters — values are always lifetime totals.

query.description: REQUIRED — site UUID as query param (not path segment)

request.description: Lifetime trading statistics: `status`, `greenEnergySavings` (EUR), `energyTraderSavings` (EUR). Values accumulate over the site's entire trading history; no date range supported.

Average monthly Energy-Trader savings (`averagePastVariableSavings` in EUR). QUIRK: the path segment is the **site ID** (= systemId), NOT the customer ID — despite the misleading URL structure. Verified live: customer_id → HTTP 403, site_id → 200.

query.description: REQUIRED — site UUID as query param (not path segment)

request.description: Financial breakdown across five aggregation windows (`day`/`week`/`month`/`halfYear`/`year`): PV production, grid feed-in, grid consumption, site totals, effective per-kWh Heartbeat price. THREE DISTINCT PRICE SEMANTICS — do not confuse: (1) `pvProduction.price` is Heartbeat's internal PV valuation (≈0.05 EUR/kWh, not a market price); (2) `gridFeedIn.price` is the contractual feed-in tariff; (3) `gridConsumption.price` is the effective per-kWh grid buy price averaged over the window; `heartbeatPrice` is the site's effective all-in price; `comparisonTariff` is the grundversorger reference. VAT convention: values presented as displayed in the app — most likely gross (VAT-inclusive), matching the German consumer convention. The `vat: 0.19` field is included but its role is undocumented.

AI optimisation decisions for the requested window. QUIRK: `data.marketPrice` values are empirically much lower than the spot price returned by `charts/market-prices` for the same timestamp (factor ~4-5) — likely the feed-in / trader-side price rather than the grid-purchase price. Not officially documented. See also `Get self-sufficiency events` for the same shape and semantic caveat.

query.description: REQUIRED. Allowed: '1W', '1M', '1Y'. Any other value → HTTP 400.

request.description: Aggregated Heartbeat-AI metrics (selfSufficiency, energyEarned, co2Saved, heartbeatPrice, peakPriceAvoided) for a resolution window. QUIRK 1: only `resolution=1M` returns all metrics — `1W` and `1Y` return only `co2Saved` + `production` + `carTravelEmission`; `selfSufficiency` and `energyEarned` come back as `null`. QUIRK 2: top-level `priceAvoided`/`batteryChargingCost`/`gridChargingCost` are empirically always `null` — the actual values sit inside the `peakPriceAvoided` block.

AI events explaining self-sufficiency outcomes — typically the granular battery-discharge trace. Same payload shape as `Get optimizations` but a **different subset** of AI activity (complementary, not redundant). QUIRK: `data.marketPrice` values are empirically much lower than the Spot price returned by `charts/market-prices` at the same timestamp — likely the feed-in / trader-side price rather than the grid-purchase price. Not officially documented.
